description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of instances across different numbers of matches (ranging from 0 to 6) in the Fair-PP synthetic dataset, which is designed to align large language models with personalized preferences grounded in social equity. The chart is divided into seven segments, each representing a match count from 0 to 6, with corresponding percentages and absolute counts. The largest segment, colored light blue, represents “6 Matches” at 27.2% (8,006 instances). The second largest, in light green, corresponds to “2 Matches” at 22.4% (6,583 instances). “1 Match” accounts for 13.8% (4,046), and “0 Matches” for 13.3% (3,910), both in pale yellow tones. Smaller segments include “3 Matches” (6.8%, 2,002, light olive), “4 Matches” (6.2%, 1,810, very light blue), and “5 Matches” (10.4%, 3,043, medium blue). Each slice is labeled with its category, percentage, and count, and the segments are arranged in descending order of size clockwise from the top. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of higher match counts, particularly 6 and 2 matches, suggesting a skewed distribution toward more aligned or preferred outcomes in the dataset.
